extracted.intended_audience: CIA senior management and program offices responsible for preparing the Agency's Annual Management Improvement Report to OMB (per OMB Circular A-44)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing the Agency Annual Management Improvement Report required by OMB Circular A-44, including assigning responsibilities, assembling content on management improvement/productivity/cost reductions, and coordinating submission to OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report due date
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annual Management Improvement Report required by OMB under OMB Circular A-44 is due 1 September 1973.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions should be issued soon to meet the deadline; there may be limited tolerance for slipping a week or two depending on OMB International Programs Division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation to a single top-level official
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency Head should delegate responsibility for the whole broad management improvement program to one "top-level official reporting directly to the Department or Agency Head."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This delegation is described in Circular A-44 as 'possibly the most significant provision or instruction.' If such an official existed previously (e.g., Executive Director-Comptroller) that person would have carried this role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspector General responsibility for review policy and organizational performance reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The Inspector General had the responsibility for the articulation of Agency management review policy and for conducting organizational performance reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As articulated here, the IG is the owner of policy articulation and performance reviews — this role should be included or reassigned explicitly in the Agency's response to A-44.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directorates' reporting of improvements and plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Directorates had the responsibility for reporting management improvement, productivity, and cost reduction accomplishments and for planning and reporting upcoming efforts in those areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each directorate must provide both retrospective accomplishments and forward-looking plans related to management improvement, productivity, and cost reductions as part of the Agency submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Finance: financial management improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Finance was charged with reporting specific financial management improvements achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial management accomplishments should be separately identified and documented by the Office of Finance for inclusion in the Agency report.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPB coordination and production role
rubrics_metrics.description: D/PPB (PPB) had the responsibility, as an operating arm of the Executive Director-Comptroller, to coordinate and produce the Agency report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPB is the likely central coordinator to collect inputs, assemble the Agency-wide report, and manage submission unless another top-level official is designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of an Agency management review policy section
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency review policy section is a required element of the A-44 submission (the memo states: 'including the Agency review policy section').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether produced centrally or by directorates, the report must contain a clear statement of Agency management review policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of records management, reports reduction, and ADP improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The A-44 report must address records management, reports reduction and ADP (automated data processing) improvements as part of the Agency-wide management improvement effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific topical areas should be reported on, prioritized, and reflected in claimed improvements and plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish priority efforts and verify claimed improvements/cost-reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency must establish priority efforts and be able to verify the claims for improvement and cost-reductions submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo asks explicitly 'who is charged with establishing priority efforts and verifying the claims for improvement and cost-reductions submitted?' — implying the report should include verifiable evidence and an accountable verifier for claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative delegation: assign responsibilities to Deputy Directors if no single official
rubrics_metrics.description: If organizational problems limit assigning authoritative responsibility for agency-wide management review to a single individual, assign responsibility to each Deputy Director for activities under his command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entails issuing a request for each Deputy Director to submit his response to the total A-44 requirement (including the Agency review policy section); the memo raises the procedural question of who initiates that call (D/PPB, DD/M&S, or other).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-wide continuing oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be someone 'overviewing the effort for the whole Agency on a continuing basis' to provide ongoing oversight of management improvement activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report and the Agency's internal arrangements should identify who will provide continuous oversight (not just one-time compilation) of records management, reports reduction, ADP improvements, and verification processes.
